title: Implement agent workflow guardrails for gmind context and verification
description: Implement the PRD-03 agent workflow slice that makes gmind context and adjacent CLI behavior usable as the required pre-edit entry point for agents. Scope is limited to the CLI workflow around gmind context <beads-id> [--depth N] plus the verification handoff signals that agents rely on before closing work. This issue should make the command output deterministic and agent-consumable, preserve --depth behavior, and surface enough issue, RTE, and related-knowledge data for an agent to load execution context before editing code. It should also define the verification-facing output contract needed for the PRD-03 workflow, rather than broad PRD03 command coverage. Related PRD sections: br-prd03-s2 and br-prd03-s3.
acceptance_criteria: 1. gmind context <id> returns a stable, readable summary that includes issue state, any available RTE status or resolution, and related knowledge required to start implementation work. 2. gmind context <id> --json returns deterministic structured fields that agents can parse without relying on debug logs or ad-hoc text scraping. 3. --depth continues to work and clearly changes how much context is included, without breaking existing successful paths. 4. Failure modes at the system boundary are explicit: missing issue, unavailable storage, or unavailable fastcode or zvec dependencies produce clear CLI errors instead of silent partial success. 5. The implementation is covered by focused tests for the workflow contract and does not require broad end-to-end PRD03 manual testing to validate basic correctness. 6. Issue metadata carries PRD traceability via labels for the relevant sections.
close_reason: QA passed: implementation verified and ready for completion.

title: feat(gmind): replace Zvec stubs with FrankenSQLite-backed storage
description: ZvecDB in cli/gmind/internal/storage/zvec.go is currently a stub: UpsertChunk only prints to stdout (no persistence), SearchByBeadsID returns hardcoded mock data, and SemanticSearch returns fake results. This makes gmind reindex and gmind context Zvec layer non-functional. Replace all three stubs with real FrankenSQLite-backed implementations: create a zvec_chunks table (chunk_id, source_type, source_ref, beads_ids, content, score, timestamp, author), implement UpsertChunk with INSERT OR REPLACE, implement SearchByBeadsID with SELECT WHERE beads_ids LIKE, and implement SemanticSearch with basic keyword matching (until C++ zvec is integrated). Satisfies: br-prd03-s1. Depends on: gmind-216 (semantic chunking).
close_reason: Implemented FrankenSQLite backend for Zvec

title: Add streaming progress output for fastcode query to prevent silent CLI hangs
description:
Currently, `gmind context <id>` invokes `fastcode query` under the hood. `fastcode query` performs an iterative LLM search which can take 4-5 rounds and upwards of 5 minutes. Because `exec.Command().CombinedOutput()` buffers the entire output, the CLI provides zero feedback to the user, appearing as a silent crash or dead hang. 

We need to:
1. Stream stdout/stderr from the `fastcode query` subprocess back to the user instead of fully buffering it until completion.
2. Provide a loading spinner/progress indicator.
3. Pass through the fastcode intermediate logging so the user knows work is actively happening.
close_reason: QA passed: implementation verified and ready for completion.

title: Implement rejected RTE guidance in gmind trace and context output
description: `gmind reject` already updates issue state and stores the rejection reason, but the CLI still treats rejected RTE data as generic metadata. Implement the missing rejected-flow presentation required by PRD-03 Section 4 so agents can clearly see that the previous approach was rejected and a new proposal is required. Scope: user-facing output in `gmind trace <id>` and `gmind context <id>` for items with `rte_status=rejected`. Acceptance criteria: (1) `gmind trace <id>` renders rejected items with explicit rejected wording, including the latest rejection reason, instead of a generic metadata line; (2) `gmind context <id>` renders a dedicated rejected RTE section for rejected items rather than the generic `RTE Metadata` heading; (3) rejected output clearly tells the next agent that a new approach is required, while approved output remains unchanged; (4) JSON fields and persisted storage schema remain backward compatible; (5) automated tests cover rejected rendering in both trace and context paths. Related to PRD-03 Section 4.
